sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tat sarvam upānayam upāhṛtam vānarān sāntvayitvā ca sarvān eva vyasarjayat
english: Having received all that had been brought and presented as tribute, and having consoled all the monkeys, he dismissed them all.

sanskrit: visarjayitvā sa harīñ śūrāṃs tān kṛtakarmaṇaḥ mene kṛtārtham ātmānaṃ rāghavaṃ ca mahābalam
english: Having dismissed those heroic monkeys who had accomplished their task, he considered both himself and the mighty Rāghava to have attained their purpose.

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇo bhīmabalaṃ sarvavānarasattamam abravīt praśritaṃ vākyaṃ sugrīvaṃ saṃpraharṣayan kiṣkindhāyā viniṣkrāma yadi te saumya rocate
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, delighting Sugrīva, spoke deferential words to that best of all monkeys possessed of terrible strength: "Come forth from Kiṣkindhā, O gentle one, if it pleases you."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇasya subhāṣitam sugrīvaḥ paramaprīto vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Hearing those well-spoken words of Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, supremely pleased, spoke these words in reply.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhavatu gacchāmaḥ stheyaṃ tvacchāsane mayā tam evam uktvā sugrīvo lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣmaṇam
english: "So be it; let us go — I must abide by your command." Having spoken thus to the auspicious-marked Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva then...

sanskrit: visarjayām āsa tadā tārām anyāś ca yoṣitaḥ etety uccair harivarān sugrīvaḥ samudāharat
english: ...dismissed Tārā and the other women at that moment. Then Sugrīva called out loudly to the foremost of the monkeys, saying "Come!"

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā harayaḥ śīghram āyayuḥ baddhāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve ye syuḥ strīdarśanakṣamāḥ
english: Hearing his command, the monkeys — all of those who were fit to appear before women — came quickly with palms joined in reverence.

sanskrit: tān uvāca tataḥ prāptān rājārkasadṛśaprabhaḥ upasthāpayata kṣipraṃ śibikāṃ mama vānarāḥ
english: To those who had arrived, the king, whose radiance resembled the sun's, then said: "Monkeys, quickly bring my palanquin forward."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya harayaḥ śīghravikramāḥ samupasthāpayām āsuḥ śibikāṃ priyadarśanām
english: Hearing his words, the monkeys of swift step at once brought forward a beautiful palanquin pleasing to behold.

sanskrit: tām upasthāpitāṃ dṛṣṭvā śibikāṃ vānarādhipaḥ lakṣmaṇāruhyatāṃ śīghram iti saumitrim abravīt
english: Seeing the palanquin brought forth, the lord of monkeys said to Saumitri: "Lakṣmaṇa, mount this quickly."

sanskrit: ity uktvā kāñcanaṃ yānaṃ sugrīvaḥ sūryasaṃnibham bṛhadbhir haribhir yuktam āruroha salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Sugrīva mounted together with Lakṣmaṇa the golden conveyance that resembled the sun, drawn by large monkeys.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani śuklaiś ca bālavyajanair dhūyamānaiḥ samantataḥ
english: A white royal parasol was held above his head, and white yak-tail fans were waved about him on all sides.

sanskrit: śaṅkhabherīninādaiś ca bandibhiś cābhivanditaḥ niryayau prāpya sugrīvo rājyaśriyam anuttamām
english: Acclaimed by bards and heralded by the sounds of conches and kettledrums, Sugrīva, having attained the unsurpassed glory of kingship, set forth.

sanskrit: sa vānaraśatais tīṣkṇair bahubhiḥ śastrapāṇibhiḥ parikīrṇo yayau tatra yatra rāmo vyavasthitaḥ
english: Surrounded by many hundreds of fierce monkeys bearing weapons in hand, he proceeded to the place where Rāma was stationed.

sanskrit: sa taṃ deśam anuprāpya śreṣṭhaṃ rāmaniṣevitam avātaran mahātejāḥ śibikāyāḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Reaching that excellent place frequented by Rāma, the great-spirited one descended from the palanquin together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: āsādya ca tato rāmaṃ kṛtāñjalipuṭo 'bhavat kṛtāñjalau sthite tasmin vānarāś cabhavaṃs tathā
english: Approaching Rāma, he stood with palms joined in reverence; and as he stood thus with joined palms, the monkeys did likewise.

sanskrit: taṭākam iva tad dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ kuḍmalapaṅkajam vānarāṇāṃ mahat sainyaṃ sugrīve prītimān abhūt
english: Seeing that vast army of monkeys — like a lake full of closed lotuses — Rāma was filled with affection for Sugrīva.

sanskrit: pādayoḥ patitaṃ mūrdhnā tam utthāpya harīśvaram preṃṇā ca bahumānāc ca rāghavaḥ pariṣasvaje
english: When the lord of monkeys fell at his feet, touching them with his head, Rāghava raised him up and embraced him with affection and deep regard.

sanskrit: pariṣvajya ca dharmātmā niṣīdeti tato 'bravīt taṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā kṣitau rāmo 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: Having embraced him, the righteous-souled one said: "Be seated." Then, seeing him seated upon the ground, Rāma spoke these words.

sanskrit: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca kāle yas tu niṣevate vibhajya satataṃ vīra sa rājā harisattama
english: "O hero, O best of monkeys — the one who constantly pursues righteousness, wealth, and pleasure each in its proper time and measure, he is a true king.

sanskrit: hitvā dharmaṃ tathārthaṃ ca kāmaṃ yas tu niṣevate sa vṛkṣāgre yathā suptaḥ patitaḥ pratibudhyate
english: But one who, abandoning righteousness and wealth alike, indulges only in pleasure, wakes to find himself fallen — like a man who fell asleep at the top of a tree.

sanskrit: amitrāṇāṃ vadhe yukto mitrāṇāṃ saṃgrahe rataḥ trivargaphalabhoktā tu rājā dharmeṇa yujyate
english: A king who is engaged in the destruction of enemies, devoted to the protection of allies, and who enjoys the fruit of the threefold human aims — he is joined to righteousness.

sanskrit: udyogasamayas tv eṣa prāptaḥ śatruvināśana saṃcintyatāṃ hi piṅgeśa haribhiḥ saha mantribhiḥ
english: The time for exertion has now arrived, O destroyer of enemies. Take counsel, O tawny-eyed lord, together with the monkeys and your ministers."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sugrīvo rāmaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed, Sugrīva spoke these words to Rāma.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭā śrīś ca kīrtiś ca kapirājyaṃ ca śāśvatam tvatprasādān mahābāho punaḥ prāptam idaṃ mayā
english: "Prosperity, fame, and the eternal kingdom of the monkeys — all of it had been lost to me, O mighty-armed one, and has been regained through your grace.

sanskrit: tava devaprasadāc ca bhrātuś ca jayatāṃ vara kṛtaṃ na pratikuryād yaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ sa dūṣakaḥ
english: By the grace of you who art as a god, and of your brother, O best among the victorious — one who does not requite a good deed done is the blight of mankind.

sanskrit: ete vānaramukhyāś ca śataśaḥ śatrusūdana prāptāś cādāya balinaḥ pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarān
english: These foremost of monkeys have arrived by hundreds, O slayer of enemies, bringing with them all the powerful monkeys of the earth.

sanskrit: ṛkṣāś cāvahitāḥ śūrā golāṅgūlāś ca rāghava kāntāra vanadurgāṇām abhijñā ghoradarśanāḥ
english: Bears too are here, watchful and heroic, O Rāghava, and the golāṅgūlas — those fearsome in appearance who know the fastnesses of wildernesses and forests.

sanskrit: devagandharvaputrāś ca vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ parivṛtāḥ sainyair vartante pathi rāghava
english: Monkeys who are sons of gods and gandharvas, who can assume any form at will, each surrounded by their own armies — they are on the march, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: śataiḥ śatasahasraiś ca koṭibhiś ca plavaṃgamāḥ ayutaiś cāvṛtā vīrā śaṅkubhiś ca paraṃtapa
english: Hundreds, hundreds of thousands, tens of millions — the leaping ones arrive; heroes encompassed by tens of thousands and by śaṅkus in number, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: arbudair arbudaśatair madhyaiś cāntaiś ca vānarāḥ samudraiś ca parārdhaiś ca harayo hariyūthapāḥ
english: By arbuda-multitudes and hundreds of arbudas, by madhyas and antas, by samudras and parārdhhas — the monkeys and monkey-troop-leaders come in such numbers.

sanskrit: āgamiṣyanti te rājan mahendrasamavikramāḥ merumandarasaṃkāśā vindhyamerukṛtālayāḥ
english: They shall come to you, O king — those whose valor matches Mahendra's, who loom like Meru and Mandara, whose abodes are on the Vindhyas and Meru.

sanskrit: te tvām abhigamiṣyanti rākṣasaṃ ye sabāndhavam nihatya rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye hy ānayiṣyanti maithilīm
english: They will come to you — having slain Rāvaṇa together with his kinsmen in battle, they will bring back the Maithilī."

sanskrit: tatas tam udyogam avekṣya buddhimān haripravīrasya nideśavartinaḥ babhūva harṣād vasudhādhipātmajaḥ prabuddhanīlotpalatulyadarśanaḥ
english: Then, beholding that readiness of the foremost monkey who stood obedient to his direction, the wise son of the earth's lord blazed with joy — his appearance equal to that of a blooming blue lotus.

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇaṃ sugrīvaṃ rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ bāhubhyāṃ saṃpariṣvajya pratyuvāca kṛtāñjalim
english: While Sugrīva spoke thus, Rāma, best among those who uphold righteousness, embraced him with both arms and replied to him who stood with palms joined.

sanskrit: yad indro varṣate varṣaṃ na tac citraṃ bhaved bhuvi ādityo vā sahasrāṃśuḥ kuryād vitimiraṃ nabhaḥ
english: "That Indra sends down rain upon the earth — that is no wonder; that Āditya of the thousand rays dispels darkness from the sky —

sanskrit: candramā raśmibhiḥ kuryāt pṛthivīṃ saumya nirmalām tvadvidho vāpi mitrāṇāṃ pratikuryāt paraṃtapa
english: that the moon with its rays purifies the earth — O gentle one, O scorcher of foes, that one like you should requite friends — none of this is a marvel.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvayi na tac citraṃ bhaved yat saumya śobhanam jānāmy ahaṃ tvāṃ sugrīva satataṃ priyavādinam
english: So also in you, whatever is noble and good is no wonder, O gentle one. I know you, Sugrīva, as one who always speaks with affection.

sanskrit: tvatsanāthaḥ sakhe saṃkhye jetāsmi sakalān arīn tvam eva me suhṛn mitraṃ sāhāyyaṃ kartum arhasi
english: With you as my protector, O friend, I shall conquer all enemies in battle. You alone are my well-wisher and ally; it is fitting that you render me aid.

sanskrit: jahārātmavināśāya vaidehīṃ rākṣasādhamaḥ vañcayitvā tu paulomīm anuhlādo yathā śacīm
english: That vilest of rākṣasas abducted the Vaidehī to his own destruction, just as Anuhlāda carried off Śacī, daughter of Puloman, by deception.

sanskrit: nacirāt taṃ haniṣyāmi rāvaṇaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ paulomyāḥ pitaraṃ dṛptaṃ śatakratur ivārihā
english: Before long I shall slay Rāvaṇa with my keen arrows, as Śatakratu, the destroyer of enemies, slew the proud father of Paulomī."

sanskrit: etasminn antare caiva rajaḥ samabhivartata uṣṇāṃ tīvrāṃ sahasrāṃśoś chādayad gagane prabhām
english: Just then a great cloud of dust arose, hot and dense, obscuring the bright radiance of the thousand-rayed sun in the sky.

sanskrit: diśaḥ paryākulāś cāsan rajasā tena mūrchitāḥ cacāla ca mahī sarvā saśailavanakānanā
english: The directions became confused and thick with that dust; the whole earth, with its mountains, forests, and groves, trembled.

sanskrit: tato nagendrasaṃkāśais tīkṣṇa daṃṣṭrair mahābalaiḥ kṛtsnā saṃchāditā bhūmir asaṃkhyeyaiḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ
english: Then the entire earth was covered over by innumerable leaping monkeys resembling mountain-peaks, possessing sharp fangs and immense strength.

sanskrit: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tatas tair hariyūthapaiḥ koṭīśataparīvāraiḥ kāmarūpibhir āvṛtā
english: In the mere twinkling of an eye, it was covered by those monkey-troop-leaders, able to assume any form at will, each attended by hundreds of crores of followers.

sanskrit: nādeyaiḥ pārvatīyaiś ca sāmudraiś ca mahābalaiḥ haribhir meghanirhrādair anyaiś ca vanacāribhiḥ
english: By monkeys of the rivers, of the mountains, and of the oceans — all of great strength, thundering like clouds — and by others who roam the forests.

sanskrit: taruṇādityavarṇaiś ca śaśigauraiś ca vānaraiḥ padmakesaravarṇaiś ca śvetair merukṛtālayaiḥ
english: By monkeys of the color of the young sun, and by those as pale as the moon; by those of the hue of lotus stamens, and by the white ones who make their home on Meru.

sanskrit: koṭīsahasrair daśabhiḥ śrīmān parivṛtas tadā vīraḥ śatabalir nāma vānaraḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Then appeared the illustrious and heroic monkey named Śatabali, surrounded by ten thousand crores of monkeys.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanaśailābhas tārāyā vīryavān pitā anekair daśasāhasraiḥ koṭibhiḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Then appeared the valorous father of Tārā, resembling a mountain of gold, with many tens of thousands of crores.

sanskrit: padmakesarasaṃkāśas taruṇārkanibhānanaḥ buddhimān vānaraśreṣṭhaḥ sarvavānarasattamaḥ
english: Of the hue of lotus stamens, with a face like the young sun — wise, the foremost of monkeys, the best of all the monkey-host —

sanskrit: anīkair bahusāhasrair vānarāṇāṃ samanvitaḥ pitā hanumataḥ śrīmān kesarī pratyadṛśyata
english: — attended by armies of many thousands of monkeys, the illustrious Kesarī, father of Hanumān, appeared.

sanskrit: golāṅgūlamahārājo gavākṣo bhīmavikramaḥ vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa vānarāṇām adṛśyata
english: The great king of the golāṅgūlas, Gavākṣa of terrible valor, appeared surrounded by a thousand crores of monkeys.

sanskrit: ṛkṣāṇāṃ bhīmavegānāṃ dhūmraḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ vṛtaḥ koṭisahasrābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ samabhivartata
english: Dhūmra, destroyer of enemies, lord of bears of terrible speed, advanced surrounded by two thousand crores.

sanskrit: mahācalanibhair ghoraiḥ panaso nāma yūthapaḥ ājagāma mahāvīryas tisṛbhiḥ koṭibhir vṛtaḥ
english: The troop-leader named Panasa, of great valor, came attended by three crores of monkeys terrible as great mountains.

sanskrit: nīlāñjanacayākāro nīlo nāmātha yūthapaḥ adṛśyata mahākāyaḥ koṭibhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ
english: The troop-leader named Nīla appeared — of the hue of a mass of blue antimony, immense of body — attended by ten crores.

sanskrit: darīmukhaś ca balavān yūthapo 'bhyāyayau tadā vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa sugrīvaṃ samupasthitaḥ
english: The powerful troop-leader Darīmukha came forth at that time, surrounded by a thousand crores, and presented himself to Sugrīva.

sanskrit: maindaś ca dvividaś cobhāv aśviputrau mahāvalau koṭikoṭisahasreṇa vānarāṇām adṛśyatām
english: Mainda and Dvivida, both sons of the Aśvins, both of immense strength, appeared with a thousand crores of crores of monkeys.

sanskrit: tataḥ koṭisahasrāṇāṃ sahasreṇa śatena ca pṛṣṭhato 'nugataḥ prāpto haribhir gandhamādanaḥ
english: Then Gandhamādana arrived, followed from behind by thousands of thousands of crores, along with hundreds of crores of monkeys.

sanskrit: tataḥ padmasahasreṇa vṛtaḥ śaṅkuśatena ca yuvarājo 'ṅgadaḥ prāptaḥ pitṛtulyaparākramaḥ
english: Then came Aṅgada the crown prince, equal to his father in valor, surrounded by a thousand padmas and a hundred śaṅkus.

sanskrit: tatas tārādyutis tāro harir bhīmaparākramaḥ pañcabhir harikoṭībhir dūrataḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Then Tāra, the monkey of terrible valor and with the radiance of a star, was seen from afar, attended by five crores of monkeys.

sanskrit: indrajānuḥ kapir vīro yūthapaḥ pratyadṛśyata ekādaśānāṃ koṭīnām īśvaras taiś ca saṃvṛtaḥ
english: The heroic monkey Indrajānu, a troop-leader, appeared as the lord of eleven crores, surrounded by them.

sanskrit: tato rambhas tv anuprāptas taruṇādityasaṃnibhaḥ ayutena vṛtaś caiva sahasreṇa śatena ca
english: Then Rambha arrived, resembling the young sun, surrounded by ten thousand along with a thousand hundreds.

sanskrit: tato yūthapatir vīro durmukho nāma vānaraḥ pratyadṛśyata koṭibhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ parivṛto balī
english: Then the heroic troop-leader, the powerful monkey named Durmukha, appeared surrounded by two crores.

sanskrit: kailāsaśikharākārair vānarair bhīmavikramaiḥ vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa hanumān pratyadṛśyata
english: Hanumān appeared, surrounded by a thousand crores of monkeys of terrible valor who resembled the peaks of Kailāsa.

sanskrit: nalaś cāpi mahāvīryaḥ saṃvṛto drumavāsibhiḥ koṭīśatena saṃprāptaḥ sahasreṇa śatena ca
english: Nala too, of great valor, surrounded by tree-dwellers, arrived with a hundred crores along with a hundred thousands.

sanskrit: śarabhaḥ kumudo vahnir vānaro rambha eva ca ete cānye ca bahavo vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: Śarabha, Kumuda, Vahni, the monkey Rambha — these and many other monkeys who could assume any form at will —

sanskrit: āvṛtya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca āplavantaḥ plavantaś ca garjantaś ca plavaṃgamāḥ abhyavartanta sugrīvaṃ sūryam abhragaṇā iva
english: — covering the whole earth, its mountains and its forests, leaping, bounding, and roaring, those leaping ones came toward Sugrīva as clouds come toward the sun.

sanskrit: kurvāṇā bahuśabdāṃś ca prahṛṣṭā balaśālinaḥ śirobhir vānarendrāya sugrīvāya nyavedayan
english: Making great clamor, joyful and strong, they presented themselves to Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, bowing their heads.

sanskrit: apare vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ saṃgamya ca yathocitam sugrīveṇa samāgamya sthitāḥ prāñjalayas tadā
english: Other foremost of monkeys, having met and saluted Sugrīva in the proper manner, stood before him with palms joined.

sanskrit: sugrīvas tvarito rāme sarvāṃs tān vānararṣabhān nivedayitvā dharmajñaḥ sthitaḥ prāñjalir abravīt
english: Swiftly Sugrīva, the righteous-minded one, introduced all those bull-like monkeys to Rāma, then stood with palms joined and spoke.

sanskrit: yathā sukhaṃ parvatanirjhareṣu vaneṣu sarveṣu ca vānarendrāḥ niveśayitvā vidhivad balāni balaṃ balajñaḥ pratipattum īṣṭe
english: "Let the lords of monkeys quarter the forces at ease in the mountain streams and all the forests; then he who knows strength, having arrayed the army properly, is ready to march."

sanskrit: atha rājā samṛddhārthaḥ sugrīvaḥ plavageśvaraḥ uvāca naraśārdūlaṃ rāmaṃ parabalārdanam
english: Then Sugrīva, lord of the leaping ones, his purpose fully achieved, spoke to Rāma, that tiger among men and crusher of enemy armies.

sanskrit: āgatā viniviṣṭāś ca balinaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ vānarendrā mahendrābhā ye madviṣayavāsinaḥ
english: "The lords of monkeys who dwell in my domain — powerful, able to assume any form at will, and resembling Mahendra — have arrived and are encamped.

sanskrit: ta ime bahusāhasrair haribhir bhīmavikramaiḥ āgatā vānarā ghorā daityadānavasaṃnibhāḥ
english: These terrible monkeys who have come, each attended by many thousands of monkeys of fearful valor, are like the Daityas and Dānavas in might.

sanskrit: khyātakarmāpadānāś ca balavanto jitaklamāḥ parākrameṣu vikhyātā vyavasāyeṣu cottamāḥ
english: Known for deeds and exploits, powerful, inured to fatigue, renowned for their valor and foremost in their undertakings —

sanskrit: pṛthivyambucarā rāma nānānaganivāsinaḥ koṭyagraśa ime prāptā vānarās tava kiṃkarāḥ
english: — wanderers of the earth and waters, O Rāma, dwellers on many mountains — these monkeys have arrived by the crore as your servants.

sanskrit: nideśavartinaḥ sarve sarve guruhite ratāḥ abhipretam anuṣṭhātuṃ tava śakṣyanty ariṃdama
english: All are obedient to command, all are devoted to the welfare of their lord; they are capable of carrying out your purpose, O subduer of enemies.

sanskrit: yan manyase naravyāghra prāptakālaṃ tad ucyatām tat sainyaṃ tvadvaśe yuktam ājñāpayitum arhasi
english: Whatever you deem timely, O tiger among men — let it be declared. This army is at your disposal; you ought to give the command."

sanskrit: kāmam eṣām idaṃ kāryaṃ viditaṃ mama tattvataḥ tathāpi tu yathā tattvam ājñāpayitum arhasi
english: "Though this task of theirs is truly known to me in its essence, even so, you ought to give the command in the proper way."

sanskrit: tathā bruvāṇaṃ sugrīvaṃ rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ bāhubhyāṃ saṃpariṣvajya idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: To Sugrīva speaking thus, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, embraced him with both arms and spoke these words.

sanskrit: jñāyatāṃ saumya vaidehī yadi jīvati vā na vā sa ca deśo mahāprājña yasmin vasati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "Let it be ascertained, O gentle one, whether the Vaidehī lives or does not live — and the place, O greatly wise one, where Rāvaṇa dwells.

sanskrit: adhigamya ca vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca prāptakālaṃ vidhāsyāmi tasmin kāle saha tvayā
english: Having found the Vaidehī and Rāvaṇa's dwelling, I shall do what is fitting in that time, together with you.

sanskrit: nāham asmin prabhuḥ kārye vānareśa na lakṣmaṇaḥ tvam asya hetuḥ kāryasya prabhuś ca plavageśvara
english: In this task, O lord of monkeys, I am not the master, nor is Lakṣmaṇa — you are both the cause and the master of this undertaking, O lord of leaping ones.

sanskrit: tvam evājñāpaya vibho mama kāryaviniścayam tvaṃ hi jānāsi yat kāryaṃ mama vīra na saṃśayaḥ
english: You yourself, O lord, must determine and direct my task; for you know what is to be done for me, O hero — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: suhṛddvitīyo vikrāntaḥ prājñaḥ kālaviśeṣavit bhavān asmaddhite yuktaḥ sukṛtārtho 'rthavittamaḥ
english: You are valorous, accompanied by a friend, wise, knowing the distinctions of time — you are engaged in our welfare, accomplished in worthy deeds and foremost among those who understand purpose."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sugrīvo vinataṃ nāma yūthapam abravīd rāma sāmnidhye lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ śailābhaṃ meghanirghoṣam ūrjitaṃ plavageśvaram
english: Thus addressed, Sugrīva spoke in the presence of Rāma and the wise Lakṣmaṇa to the troop-leader named Vinata — that lord of leaping ones, mountain-like, thundering like a cloud, and mighty.

sanskrit: somasūryātmajaiḥ sārdhaṃ vānarair vānarottama deśakālanayair yuktaḥ kāryākāryaviniścaye
english: "O foremost of monkeys, accompanied by monkeys who are sons of Soma and Sūrya, guided by policy suited to place and time, adept at distinguishing what ought and ought not to be done —

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ śatasahasreṇa vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām adhigaccha diśaṃ pūrvāṃ saśailavanakānanām
english: — attended by one hundred thousand swift-moving monkeys, go and search the eastern direction with its mountains, forests, and groves.

sanskrit: tatra sītāṃ ca vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca mārgadhvaṃ giridurgeṣu vaneṣu ca nadīṣu ca
english: There, search for Sītā the Vaidehī and for Rāvaṇa's dwelling in the mountain fastnesses, in the forests, and in the rivers.

sanskrit: nadīṃ bhāgīrathīṃ ramyāṃ sarayūṃ kauśikīṃ tathā kālindīṃ yamunāṃ ramyāṃ yāmunaṃ ca mahāgirim
english: The lovely Bhāgīrathī, the Sarayū, the Kauśikī, the Kālindī, the lovely Yamunā, and the great mountain Yāmuna —

sanskrit: sarasvatīṃ ca sindhuṃ ca śoṇaṃ maṇinibhodakam mahīṃ kālamahīṃ caiva śailakānanaśobhitām
english: — the Sarasvatī and the Sindhu; the Śona with its gem-bright waters; the Mahī and the Kālamahī adorned with hills and forests —

sanskrit: brahmamālān videhāṃś ca mālavān kāśikosalān māgadhāṃś ca mahāgrāmān puṇḍrān vaṅgāṃs tathaiva ca
english: — the Brahmamālas, the Videhas, the Mālavas, the Kāśi-Kosalas; the Māgadhas with their great towns; the Puṇḍras and the Vaṅgas as well —

sanskrit: pattanaṃ kośakārāṇāṃ bhūmiṃ ca rajatākarām sarvam etad vicetavyaṃ mṛgayadbhir tatas tataḥ
english: — the city of the silk-worm workers and the land rich in silver mines — all this must be searched through, ranging here and there in your quest.

sanskrit: rāmasya dayitāṃ bhāryāṃ sītāṃ daśarataḥ snuṣām samudram avagāḍhāś ca parvatān pattanāni ca
english: Search for Sītā, the dear wife of Rāma and daughter-in-law of Daśaratha — in the seas, on the mountains, and in the cities.

sanskrit: mandarasya ca ye koṭiṃ saṃśritāḥ ke cid āyatām karṇaprāvaraṇāś caiva tathā cāpy oṣṭhakarṇakāḥ
english: And those who inhabit the high ridge of Mandara — those who use their ears as coverings, and those with lip-ears too —

sanskrit: ghorā lohamukhāś caiva javanāś caikapādakāḥ akṣayā balavantaś ca puruṣāḥ puruṣādakāḥ
english: — the terrible iron-mouthed ones, the swift one-footed ones, the inexhaustible and powerful men-eaters —

sanskrit: kirātāḥ karṇacūḍāś ca hemāṅgāḥ priyadarśanāḥ āmamīnāśanās tatra kirātā dvīpavāsinaḥ
english: — Kirātas with topknot-ears, golden-limbed, beautiful to behold; Kirātas who eat raw fish, dwelling there on islands —

sanskrit: antarjalacarā ghorā naravyāghrā iti śrutāḥ eteṣām ālayāḥ sarve viceyāḥ kānanaukasaḥ
english: — those terrible ones known as tiger-men who range beneath the waters — all the forest-dwellings of these must be searched.

sanskrit: giribhir ye ca gamyante plavanena plavena ca ratnavantaṃ yavadvīpaṃ saptarājyopaśobhitam
english: And those places reached by mountains, or by swimming, or by boat — Yavadvīpa, rich in gems, adorned with seven kingdoms —

sanskrit: suvarṇarūpyakaṃ caiva suvarṇākaramaṇḍitam yavadvīpam atikramya śiśiro nāma parvataḥ
english: — rich in gold and silver, ornamented with mines of gold. Beyond Yavadvīpa is a mountain named Śiśira —

sanskrit: divaṃ spṛśati śṛṅgeṇa devadānavasevitaḥ eteṣāṃ giridurgeṣu pratāpeṣu vaneṣu ca
english: — whose peak touches the sky, frequented by gods and dānavas. In the fastnesses of these mountains, their sun-scorched heights, and their forests —

sanskrit: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ tataḥ samudradvīpāṃś ca subhīmān draṣṭum arhatha
english: — Rāvaṇa with the Vaidehī must be searched for, here and there. Then you must look upon the ocean-islands, so dreadful to behold.

sanskrit: tatrāsurā mahākāyāś chāyāṃ gṛhṇanti nityaśaḥ brahmaṇā samanujñātā dīrghakālaṃ bubhukṣitāḥ
english: There, asuras of great body, who are perpetually hungry and have been so permitted by Brahmā, ever seize upon shadows.

sanskrit: taṃ kālameghapratimaṃ mahoraganiṣevitam abhigamya mahānādaṃ tīrthenaiva mahodadhim
english: Approaching the great ocean, which roars loudly and resembles a dark rain-cloud, by a proper ford — that sea frequented by great serpents —

sanskrit: tato raktajalaṃ bhīmaṃ lohitaṃ nāma sāgaram gatā drakṣyatha tāṃ caiva bṛhatīṃ kūṭaśālmalīm
english: — going onward, you shall see the dread Lohita ocean with its blood-red waters, and also the great Kūṭaśālmalī tree.

sanskrit: gṛhaṃ ca vainateyasya nānāratnavibhūṣitam tatra kailāsasaṃkāśaṃ vihitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: And there too is the dwelling of Vainateya, adorned with manifold jewels, white as Kailāsa, fashioned by Viśvakarman.

sanskrit: tatra śailanibhā bhīmā mandehā nāma rākṣasāḥ śailaśṛṅgeṣu lambante nānārūpā bhayāvahāḥ
english: There, rākṣasas named Mandehas, terrible and mountain-like, of many forms and inspiring terror, hang from the mountain-peaks.

sanskrit: te patanti jale nityaṃ sūryasyodayanaṃ prati abhitaptāś ca sūryeṇa lambante sma punaḥ punaḥ
english: They fall into the water every day at the sun's rising, and, scorched by the sun, they hang again and again.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāṇḍurameghābhaṃ kṣīraudaṃ nāma sāgaram gatā drakṣyatha durdharṣā mukhā hāram ivormibhiḥ
english: Then, advancing, you shall see the Kṣīroda ocean, resembling a pale-white cloud, whose waves make it like a garland — a formidable sight.

sanskrit: tasya madhye mahāśveta ṛṣabho nāma parvataḥ divyagandhaiḥ kusumitai rajataiś ca nagair vṛtaḥ
english: In its midst stands a great white mountain named Ṛṣabha, surrounded by silver trees in blossom with divine fragrances.

sanskrit: saraś ca rājataiḥ padmair jvalitair hemakesaraiḥ nāmnā sudarśanaṃ nāma rājahaṃsaiḥ samākulam
english: And there is a lake named Sudarśana, filled with silver lotuses blazing with golden stamens, thronged with royal swans.

sanskrit: vibudhāś cāraṇā yakṣāḥ kiṃnarāḥ sāpsarogaṇāḥ hṛṣṭāḥ samabhigacchanti nalinīṃ tāṃ riraṃsavaḥ
english: The vibudhas, cāraṇas, yakṣas, kiṃnaras, and hosts of apsarases, joyful and desirous of sport, all frequent that lotus-lake.

sanskrit: kṣīrodaṃ samatikramya tato drakṣyatha vānarāḥ jalodaṃ sāgaraśreṣṭhaṃ sarvabhūtabhayāvaham
english: Passing beyond the Kṣīroda, you will then see, O monkeys, the Jaloda, foremost of oceans and inspiring fear in all creatures.

sanskrit: tatra tat kopajaṃ tejaḥ kṛtaṃ hayamukhaṃ mahat asyāhus tan mahāvegam odanaṃ sacarācaram
english: There, they say, resides that great fire born of wrath, which has been given the form of a horse's mouth — that one of tremendous speed, which consumes all things moving and still.

sanskrit: tatra vikrośatāṃ nādo bhūtānāṃ sāgaraukasām śrūyate cāsamarthānāṃ dṛṣṭvā tad vaḍavāmukham
english: There the cries of ocean-dwelling creatures are heard — of those unable to endure what they see — upon beholding that submarine mare-fire.

sanskrit: svādūdasyottare deśe yojanāni trayodaśa jātarūpaśilo nāma mahān kanakaparvataḥ
english: To the north of the sweet-water ocean, thirteen yojanas away, stands a great golden mountain named Jātarūpaśila.

sanskrit: āsīnaṃ parvatasyāgre sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam sahasraśirasaṃ devam anantaṃ nīlavāsasaṃ
english: Seated on the peak of that mountain, adored by all beings, is the god Ananta of a thousand heads, clothed in blue garments.

sanskrit: triśirāḥ kāñcanaḥ ketus tālas tasya mahātmanaḥ sthāpitaḥ parvatasyāgre virājati savedikaḥ
english: The three-headed golden banner in the form of a palmyra palm, planted atop that mountain by that great soul, shines with its altar.

sanskrit: pūrvasyāṃ diśi nirmāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tat tridaśeśvaraiḥ tataḥ paraṃ hemamayaḥ śrīmān udayaparvataḥ
english: That construction in the eastern direction was made by the lords of the thirty gods; beyond it stands the glorious Udaya mountain made of gold.

sanskrit: tasya koṭir divaṃ spṛṣṭvā śatayojanam āyatā jātarūpamayī divyā virājati savedikā
english: Its peak, touching the sky and extending a hundred yojanas, shines with a divine altar made of pure gold.

sanskrit: sālais tālais tamālaiś ca karṇikāraiś ca puṣpitaiḥ jātarūpamayair divyaiḥ śobhate sūryasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: It is adorned with śāla, tāla, tamāla, and flowering karṇikāra trees — all made of pure gold, divine, and resembling the sun.

sanskrit: tatra yojanavistāram ucchritaṃ daśayojanam śṛṅgaṃ saumanasaṃ nāma jātarūpamayaṃ dhruvam
english: There stands a certain peak named Saumanasa, one yojana in breadth and ten yojanas in height, immovably made of pure gold.

sanskrit: tatra pūrvaṃ padaṃ kṛtvā purā viṣṇus trivikrame dvitīyaṃ śikharaṃ meroś cakāra puruṣottamaḥ
english: There Viṣṇu, the supreme among persons, in the ancient act of his triple-stride, placed his first step; his second stride he placed on the peak of Meru.

sanskrit: uttareṇa parikramya jambūdvīpaṃ divākaraḥ dṛśyo bhavati bhūyiṣṭhaṃ śikharaṃ tan mahocchrayam
english: The sun, moving northward to circuit Jambūdvīpa, is most fully visible from that towering peak.

sanskrit: tatra vaikhānasā nāma vālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ prakāśamānā dṛśyante sūryavarṇās tapasvinaḥ
english: There the great sages called Vaikhānasas and Vālakhilyas, of solar radiance, glowing with ascetic power, may be seen.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sudarśano dvīpaḥ puro yasya prakāśate yasmiṃs tejaś ca cakṣuś ca sarvaprānabhṛtām api
english: In front of it shines Sudarśana island — the very place which is the light and the sight of all living beings.

sanskrit: śailasya tasya kuñjeṣu kandareṣu vaneṣu ca rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ
english: In the thickets, caves, and forests of that mountain, Rāvaṇa along with the Vaidehī must be searched for, here and there.

sanskrit: kāñcanasya ca śailasya sūryasya ca mahātmanaḥ āviṣṭā tejasā saṃdhyā pūrvā raktā prakāśate
english: Pervaded by the energy of that golden mountain and of the great-souled sun, the eastern twilight shines red.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramagamyā syād dik pūrvā tridaśāvṛtā rahitā candrasūryābhyām adṛśyā timirāvṛtā
english: Beyond that, the eastern direction becomes impassable — encircled by the thirty gods, void of sun and moon, invisible, enveloped in darkness.

sanskrit: śaileṣu teṣu sarveṣu kandareṣu vaneṣu ca ya ca noktā mayā deśā viceyā teṣu jānakī
english: In all those mountains, caves, and forests, and in those regions not named by me, Jānakī must be searched for in all of them.

sanskrit: etāvad vānaraiḥ śakyaṃ gantuṃ vānarapuṃgavāḥ abhāskaram amaryādaṃ na jānīmas tataḥ param
english: This far, O bull-like monkeys, is it possible for monkeys to go. What lies beyond — sunless and boundless — we do not know.

sanskrit: adhigamya tu vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca māse pūrṇe nivartadhvam udayaṃ prāpya parvatam
english: When you have found the Vaidehī and Rāvaṇa's dwelling, return when the month is full, having reached the Udaya mountain.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ māsān na vastavyaṃ vasan vadhyo bhaven mama siddhārthāḥ saṃnivartadhvam adhigamya ca maithilīm
english: Beyond the month, none may remain — one who dwells beyond it shall be slain by my order. Having accomplished your purpose and found the Maithilī, return.

sanskrit: mahendrakāntāṃ vanaṣaṇḍa maṇḍitāṃ diśaṃ caritvā nipuṇena vānarāḥ avāpya sītāṃ raghuvaṃśajapriyāṃ tato nivṛttāḥ sukhito bhaviṣyatha
english: Monkeys, having searched that direction beloved of Mahendra, adorned with forest thickets, with skill and care — having found Sītā, the beloved of the scion of the Raghu lineage, and then returned, you shall be happy."
